newsitem.title: USA: IPOs hit $36 billion mark, top '93 record.
newsitem.headline: IPOs hit $36 billion mark, top '93 record.

text.p: Initial public offerings of stocks have already shattered their 1993 annual record, raising over $36 billion for issuing firms so far this year, despite a sluggish third quarter.
This week promises to keep underwriters busy adding to the record, with about 30 companies heading to market.
"We should have a home run or two," said IPO Aftermarket newsletter editor John Fitzgibbon.
New equity issues raised $33 billion in 1993.
IPO proceeds fell about 60 percent in the third quarter to about $7.9 billion from nearly $19 billion in the second quarter.
Merrill Lynch & Co. led underwriters in the quarter in dollar volume, raising $996 million in proceeds from 10 deals.
Morgan Stanley came in a distant second with $567 million from eight IPOs and Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette raised $540 million with three deals.
"(The 1996 third quarter) was an about-face in IPO issuance," said Richard Peterson of Securities Data Co, which tracks equity and debt financing.
In terms of performance, William Blair & Co. was the top underwriter over the past 12 months, according to IPO Aftermarket newsletter.
"Their deals have performed the best in the aftermarket," editor Fitzgibbon said, with 11 issues gaining 75 percent over issue price on average.
However, overall performance in 1996 fell short of 1995 levels, Fitzgibbon said.
He said 631 deals priced so far had an average gain of 22.7 percent for the nine months ending Sept. 30. At this point last year, fewer deals priced, 575, but posted average gains of 39.4 percent.
Among this week's offerings, Fitzgibbon said, DIGEX Inc., a Washington, D.C., internet carrier, could rise two to three points after it opens for trading.
ArQule Inc. could also be a strong first-day performer, he said. ArQule develops and identifies chemical compounds that it sells to the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries.
The company will offer two million shares to price in an estimated range of $11 to $13.
In addition to Digex, Vince Slavin, who tracks IPOs for Cantor Fitzgerald, favours Alyn Corp., AMERISAFE Inc., XLConnect, Transkaryotic Therapies Inc. and Summit Design Inc.
Summit's software lets integrated circuit systems test their products, aiming to bring them to the market faster and at lower product cost.
Hair colour maker Carson Inc. and Metrogolf, which builds golf courses in major metropolitan areas, are also going public this week.
Laidlaw is the lead underwriter of Metrogolf's offering, which could fetch a premium of about 3/4 of a point in the aftermarket, Fitzgibbon said.
The company has negotiated a lease to build a golf range above the giant Port Authority bus station in New York City.
